dedupe_keys.name: rapidliq software for near real time prediction of soil liquefaction

description: RapidLiq: Software for Near-Real-Time Prediction of Soil Liquefaction is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Brett Maurer, University of Washington (washington.edu). RapidLiq is a Windows software program for predicting liquefaction-induced ground failure using geospatial models, which are particularly suited for regional scale applications such as: (i) loss estimation and disaster simulation; (ii) city planning and policy development; (iii) emergency response; and (d) post-event reconnaissance (e.g., to remotely identify sites of interest). Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-4bka-y039. Keywords: soil liquefaction, geospatial modelling, near-real-time prediction. Published 2021-07-26. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is GPL-3.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
